OpenRocket MIT — Flight computer and simulation API

Flight computer and MIT simulation extensions

The flight-computer runtime now lives under edu.mit.rocket_team. Its existing functional subpackages are retained. The former .zephyrus namespace segment has been removed; direct imports must use the new names.

This reference includes private implementation methods, the graphical FC designer, controller blocks, recovery, telemetry/replay, ensembles, motor batches and 3D plotting. Selected existing OpenRocket engine classes are included to make integration links navigable.

See the architecture guide for editable UML diagrams, clock/coordinate contracts and regeneration instructions.

Simulation time is virtual. Custom Java boards do not model communications contention or shared processor timing. Hardware adapters such as camera, flash and power are logical models. The documentation describes the implementation; it does not qualify physical flight hardware.

Packages
Package
Description
edu.mit.rocket_team.AV
Logical camera and video-transmitter adapters.
edu.mit.rocket_team.control
Firmware roll control and six-channel logical recovery pulse/status handling.
edu.mit.rocket_team.control.airbrakes
The airbrake predictor included by the flight-computer sketch, including its measurement buffers and preparation/control state machine.
edu.mit.rocket_team.FC
Per-run flight-computer state, firmware sequencing, virtual execution settings and PWM-latched outputs.
edu.mit.rocket_team.instrument
Engineering-unit sensor adapters with firmware filtering, zeroing and integration.
edu.mit.rocket_team.internal
Logical flash and power-board adapters used by the translated sketch.
edu.mit.rocket_team.telemetry
Ground-station-compatible packet encoding/decoding, deterministic packet loss and latency, and streaming run output.
edu.mit.rocket_team.util
Common instrument/controller interfaces, firmware state codes, virtual clock/log utilities and the bridge to per-run rocket actuators.
edu.mit.rocket_team.util.data
Mutable engineering-unit payloads at the simulator-to-instrument boundary and firmware recovery status codes.
edu.mit.rocket_team.util.hardware
Compatibility adapters for firmware hardware APIs.
